question:
Change the following sentence into positive degree.

Mercury is the smallest planet in the solar system.
option_1: Mercury is smaller than any other planet in the solar system.
option_2: No other planet is as small as Mercury in the Solar System.
option_3: Mercury is the smallest planet than any other one.
option_4: The most smallest planet in the solar system is mercury.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. No other planet is as small as Mercury in the Solar System.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence is in the superlative degree ("the smallest planet"). To convert a superlative sentence into the positive degree, the standard structure is:

◦ No other + singular noun + is + as/so + positive adjective + as + subject.

◦ Superlative: Mercury is the smallest planet in the solar system.

◦ Positive: No other planet is as small as Mercury in the Solar System.

• Option 2 follows this structure exactly and keeps the original meaning intact — that Mercury is smaller than every other planet. (बुध सौरमंडल का सबसे छोटा ग्रह है)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Mercury is smaller than any other planet..." is the comparative degree, not the positive degree, so it is not the required transformation.

• Option 3 "the smallest planet than any other one" mixes a superlative with "than" — a clear grammatical error, because "than" goes with the comparative degree.

• Option 4 "The most smallest" is a double superlative ("most" + "-est"), which is always wrong; it also wrongly writes the proper noun "Mercury" in lowercase.

NOTE

• The three standard degree transformations of the same idea:

◦ Positive: No other planet is as small as Mercury.

◦ Comparative: Mercury is smaller than any other planet.

◦ Superlative: Mercury is the smallest planet.

• Rule reminders: use "as ... as" in the positive degree, "-er/more ... than" in the comparative degree and "the ... -est/the most" in the superlative degree. Never combine "more/most" with "-er/-est".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

Thousands of people were killed by the train accident that took place last Wednesday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. killed in.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When we speak of people dying because of an event or a mishap (an accident, a blast, a fire, an earthquake, a war), the correct preposition is "in", not "by".

◦ Correct: Thousands of people were killed in the train accident that took place last Wednesday.

• "by" is used for the doer/agent of the action (killed by a tiger, killed by the robbers), whereas "in" is used for the event or place in which the deaths occurred. A train accident is an event, not an agent, so "killed in" is required. (दुर्घटना में मारे गए)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "killed of" is wrong — "of" is used with a disease/cause in "died of cancer", not with "killed".

• Option 3 "killed to" and Option 4 "killed from" are not standard collocations in English.

NOTE

• Useful collocations for SSC exams: die of (a disease — died of malaria), die from (an injury/external cause — died from a head injury), die in (an event — died in the crash), killed by (an agent — killed by a snake), killed in (an event — killed in the riots).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a spelling error.

This item is in the public domain / and can be used, / copied and modefied / without any restrictions.
option_4: This item is in the public domain
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. copied and modefied.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "modefied" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "modified", the past participle of the verb "modify", which means to change or alter something slightly. (संशोधित करना)

◦ Correct: This item is in the public domain and can be used, copied and modified without any restrictions.

• Spelling key: MO + DI + FIED. Verbs ending in consonant + y change the "y" to "i" before "-ed": modify → modified, carry → carried, apply → applied.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other three segments are correct: "This item is in the public domain", "and can be used," and "without any restrictions" contain no spelling mistakes.

• "Public domain" means material that is free from copyright and may be used by anyone.

NOTE

• Word family: modify (verb), modified (adjective/past participle), modification (noun), modifier (a word that qualifies another word). Commonly confused SSC spellings of this pattern: satisfied, justified, magnified, qualified.

question:
Select the most appropriate option with the correct usage of the preposition to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

World Press Freedom Day will be dedicated to the importance of journalism and freedom in expression in the context of the current global environmental crisis.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. freedom of expression.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed and standard phrase is "freedom of expression", meaning the right to express one's opinions and ideas freely. The noun "freedom" is normally followed by the preposition "of" when the thing that is free is named. (अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता)

◦ Correct: ... the importance of journalism and freedom of expression in the context of the current global environmental crisis.

• "freedom in expression" is not an accepted collocation in English.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "freedom from expression" reverses the sense — "freedom from" means *release from something unpleasant* (freedom from fear, freedom from hunger).

• Options 2 "freedom on expression" and 4 "freedom at expression" are not valid English collocations.

NOTE

• Common "freedom" collocations: freedom of speech / expression / religion / the press / choice; freedom from fear / want / oppression; freedom to do something.

• Static point: World Press Freedom Day is observed on 3 May every year, proclaimed by the UN General Assembly in 1993. In India, freedom of speech and expression is guaranteed by Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

In the beauty contest, Parul won the award for being the beautiful one.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. most beautiful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The definite article "the" placed before the adjective signals the superlative degree. Since Parul won the award in a beauty contest, she must have been judged the most beautiful among all the contestants.

◦ Correct: In the beauty contest, Parul won the award for being the most beautiful one.

• "Beautiful" is a long (three-syllable) adjective, so its superlative is formed with "the most" — not "beautifullest". (सबसे सुंदर)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "the least beautiful" contradicts the sense — no one wins a beauty award for being the least beautiful.

• Options 2 "more beautiful" and 4 "less beautiful" are comparative forms and would require "than" plus a second element, which is missing here.

NOTE

• Degrees of "beautiful": beautiful – more beautiful (than) – the most beautiful.

• Rule: adjectives of one syllable take -er/-est (tall, taller, tallest); adjectives of two or more syllables usually take more/most (careful, more careful, most careful).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Caught in a time warp
option_1: To avoid talking about what’s important
option_2: To remain unchanged from a time in the past
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To remain unchanged from a time in the past.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "caught in a time warp" means to remain exactly the same as in an earlier period, as if time had stopped; to be old-fashioned and untouched by change. (समय के साथ न बदलना / पुराने ज़माने में अटका रहना)

◦ Example: That sleepy little village seems caught in a time warp — the shops look exactly as they did fifty years ago.

• A "time warp" is an imaginary distortion of time in which the past and the present get mixed up, so anything "caught" in it appears frozen in an earlier era.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "To avoid talking about what's important" is the sense of idioms such as "beat about the bush".

• Option 3 "To make extra effort" corresponds to "go the extra mile" or "bend over backwards".

• Option 4 "To be extremely happy" corresponds to "on cloud nine", "over the moon" or "in seventh heaven".

NOTE

• Related time idioms frequently asked in SSC exams: behind the times (old-fashioned), ahead of one's time (having modern ideas too early), in the nick of time (just in time), against the clock (in a hurry to finish), once in a blue moon (very rarely).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The library books were long __________________, their pages bearing the weight of the passage of time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. overdue.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Overdue" is an adjective meaning not returned, paid or done by the expected time; late. Library books that were not returned on the due date are "long overdue". (नियत समय से विलंबित)

◦ Correct: The library books were long overdue, their pages bearing the weight of the passage of time.

• The clue lies in "the passage of time" — the books had been kept far beyond their return date.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "overdate" is not a standard English word in this sense.

• Option 2 "overdo" is a verb meaning to do something to excess (don't overdo the exercise) and cannot follow "were long".

• Option 3 "overdrew" is the past tense of "overdraw" — to withdraw more money than one's bank balance (he overdrew his account).

NOTE

• Common uses: an overdue book / an overdue payment / an overdue apology; "long overdue" means something should have happened much earlier. Related noun: overdue fine charged by libraries.

question: The bat flew silently through the night, searching for insects to eat. The bat in this context refers to _______.
option_1: a wooden tool utilised in sports like baseball or cricket
option_2: the act of delivering a forceful strike or hit
option_3: a measurement unit in digital information systems
option_4: a mammal known for nocturnal flight and insect consumption
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. a mammal known for nocturnal flight and insect consumption.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "bat" is a homonym — one spelling with several unrelated meanings. The correct meaning must be decided from the context.

• The context words here are "flew silently through the night" and "searching for insects to eat". Only a living creature can fly and eat insects, so "bat" here is the nocturnal flying mammal. (चमगादड़)

◦ Correct: The bat (the animal) flew silently through the night, searching for insects to eat.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (a wooden tool used in cricket/baseball) is the sporting sense of "bat" — it cannot fly or eat.

• Option 2 (a forceful strike) is the verb sense, as in "he batted the ball away".

• Option 3 refers to "bit" (binary digit), not "bat", and is therefore irrelevant.

NOTE

• The bat is the only mammal capable of true, sustained flight; it is nocturnal and navigates by echolocation.

• Other common homonyms tested in SSC exams: bark (tree covering / dog's sound), bank (river side / financial institution), spring (season / coil / water source), match (a game / a matchstick), left (past of leave / opposite of right).

question:
Select the most appropriate present tense form of the verb to fill in the blank.

They __________ football every day.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. play.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adverb phrase "every day" indicates a habitual/routine action, which requires the simple present tense.

• The subject "They" is plural, so the verb must take the plural (base) form without "-s" — "play".

◦ Correct: They play football every day.

• Subject–verb agreement rule: a singular subject takes the "-s/-es" form (He plays), while a plural subject takes the base form (They play). (वे रोज़ फुटबॉल खेलते हैं)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "plays" is the singular verb form and does not agree with the plural subject "They".

• Option 3 "had been playing" is the past perfect continuous tense, not the present tense demanded by the question.

• Option 4 "will play" is the simple future tense and again does not satisfy the "present tense" requirement.

NOTE

• Time markers for the simple present: every day, daily, usually, often, always, generally, sometimes, never, twice a week.

• Simple present is used for habits, routines, universal truths and timetables — "The sun rises in the east", "The train leaves at 6 p.m.".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I remember________ when she used to wash dishes in a restaurant.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. the time.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The clause that follows begins with "when she used to wash dishes", which refers to a period in the past. The noun that logically precedes such a "when" clause is "the time".

◦ Correct: I remember the time when she used to wash dishes in a restaurant.

• "Remember the time when ..." is a very common English structure used to recall a past occasion. (वह समय याद है जब ...)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "the business", 3 "the area" and 4 "the profile" are nouns of place/occupation and cannot be followed naturally by a "when" clause of time.

• Note the structure "used to + V1", which expresses a past habit that no longer continues.

NOTE

• Relative adverbs and the nouns they follow: when → time/day/year, where → place/house/city, why → reason. Example: "This is the place where we met", "That is the reason why he left".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Dolphins are named among the intelligent animals on earth.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. most intelligent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "among the ..." (like "one of the ...") ranks the subject within a top group, and therefore requires the superlative degree.

◦ Correct: Dolphins are named among the most intelligent animals on earth.

• "Intelligent" is a four-syllable adjective, so its superlative is formed with "most", not with the suffix "-est". (सबसे बुद्धिमान)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "intelligenter" and Option 4 "intelligentest" are non-existent forms; long adjectives never take "-er/-est".

• Option 3 "more intelligent" is the comparative and would need "than" plus a second element, which the sentence does not have.

NOTE

• Structures that demand the superlative: "one of the most ...", "among the most ...", "the ...-est ... in/of".

• Degrees of "intelligent": intelligent – more intelligent – most intelligent. Similar long adjectives: beautiful, important, difficult, expensive, dangerous.

question: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
option_1: After a tiring day, I had a cup of coffee with Sudhir.
option_2: There is a man sitting beside cat.
option_3: She saw an excellent episode of the series.
option_4: She asked an easy question, and I took an hour to crack it.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. There is a man sitting beside cat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The singular countable noun "cat" cannot stand alone without a determiner. It needs an article — "a cat" or "the cat".

◦ Incorrect: There is a man sitting beside cat.

◦ Correct: There is a man sitting beside a cat / the cat.

• Rule: every singular countable noun must be preceded by an article (a/an/the) or another determiner (this, my, one, each, etc.). (एकवचन गणनीय संज्ञा से पहले article ज़रूरी है)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is correct: "a tiring day", "a cup of coffee" — articles correctly used with singular countable nouns.

• Option 3 is correct: "an excellent episode" — "an" is used before a vowel sound (e-x-cellent).

• Option 4 is correct: "an easy question", "an hour" — "hour" begins with a silent "h", so it takes "an".

NOTE

• Article rules for SSC: use "a" before a consonant sound (a university, a European, a one-rupee note), "an" before a vowel sound (an hour, an honest man, an MP, an X-ray), and "the" for something specific or already mentioned.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.

My teacher's _______ (stern) warning made all the students quiet and calm.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. strict.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Stern" means serious, severe and strict in manner or attitude; showing disapproval and not allowing disobedience. Its closest synonym is "strict". (कठोर / सख्त)

◦ Correct: My teacher's strict warning made all the students quiet and calm.

• The result clause — "made all the students quiet and calm" — confirms that the warning was firm and severe.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "watchful" means observant/alert; it describes attention, not severity.

• Option 3 "biased" means prejudiced or unfairly favouring one side — unrelated to the sense of "stern".

• Option 4 "pliant" means flexible, easily bent or easily influenced — the opposite of stern.

NOTE

• Synonyms of stern: strict, severe, harsh, rigorous, austere, unyielding, grim.

• Antonyms of stern: lenient, gentle, kind, mild, soft, pliant, indulgent.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I will try to _______ because he is a good friend of mine.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. get him off the hook.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "get/let someone off the hook" means to help someone escape from a difficult situation, blame or punishment. (किसी को मुसीबत/दोष से बचाना)

◦ Correct: I will try to get him off the hook because he is a good friend of mine.

• The reason clause "because he is a good friend of mine" clearly signals helping the person, so only a helpful idiom fits.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "avoid him like the plague" means to keep completely away from someone — the opposite of helping a good friend.

• Option 3 "show him the door" means to dismiss someone or ask them to leave — again unfriendly.

• Option 4 "stop him in his tracks" means to make someone halt suddenly — it does not fit the sense of friendship.

NOTE

• Related idioms of rescue/help: bail someone out (rescue from trouble, especially financially), come to someone's rescue, give someone a hand, stick one's neck out for someone.

• The image behind "off the hook" comes from a fish escaping the angler's hook.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

Samira is a lady who needs extrinsic motivation and will not work on her own.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Outward.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Extrinsic" means coming from outside; external, not part of the essential nature of something. Its closest synonym among the options is "outward" (external/coming from outside). (बाहरी / बहिर्जात)

◦ Example: Rewards and praise are forms of extrinsic (outward) motivation, whereas curiosity is intrinsic motivation.

• The sentence itself explains the meaning — Samira "will not work on her own", i.e., she needs a push from outside.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Amicable" means friendly and peaceable (an amicable settlement).

• Option 3 "Intriguing" means fascinating and arousing curiosity.

• Option 4 "Adventurous" means willing to take risks and try new experiences.

NOTE

• Extrinsic vs Intrinsic: extrinsic = external, from outside (money, prizes, praise); intrinsic = internal, inherent (interest, satisfaction, passion).

• Synonyms of extrinsic: outward, external, exterior, extraneous, superficial. Antonyms: intrinsic, inherent, innate, inborn.

question:
Identify the word with a spelling error in the following sentence. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

She had swam the English Channel twice.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. swum.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the auxiliary "had" (past perfect tense), the past participle (V3) must be used.

• The verb forms of "swim" are: swim (V1) – swam (V2) – swum (V3). Since the sentence has "had", the correct form is "swum", not "swam".

◦ Incorrect: She had swam the English Channel twice.

◦ Correct: She had swum the English Channel twice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "swim" is the base form (V1) and cannot follow "had".

• Option 2 "swimming" is the present participle used with "be" (is/was swimming), not with "had".

• Option 3 "swimmed" is a non-existent form; "swim" is an irregular verb and does not take "-ed".

NOTE

• Structure: had + V3 (past perfect) is used for an action completed before another past action or before a past point of time.

• Similar irregular verbs of this pattern: sing – sang – sung, ring – rang – rung, drink – drank – drunk, begin – began – begun, sink – sank – sunk, shrink – shrank – shrunk.

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.

She recieved a beautiful surprise from her partner.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Received.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the given sentence the word is printed as "recieved", which is a misspelling. The correct spelling is "received" — the past tense of "receive", meaning to get or be given something. (प्राप्त करना)

◦ Incorrect: She recieved a beautiful surprise from her partner.

◦ Correct: She received a beautiful surprise from her partner.

• Spelling key: the classic rule "i before e, except after c" — since the letter before is "c", the order is "ce-i": re-cei-ved.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other three words in the sentence — "beautiful", "surprise" and "partner" — are all spelt correctly.

• "Surprise" is often misspelt as "suprise" (the first "r" is dropped); "beautiful" is often misspelt as "beautifull" (double "l").

NOTE

• Words following "i before e except after c": receive, deceive, conceive, perceive, ceiling — but believe, achieve, relieve, niece, piece.

• Well-known exceptions to the rule: seize, weird, either, neither, foreign, height, leisure.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The teacher asked us to _________ our homework by tomorrow.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. complete.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank comes immediately after the preposition "to", which here is part of the to-infinitive (asked us to ...). After the infinitive marker "to", the verb must be in its base form (V1).

◦ Correct: The teacher asked us to complete our homework by tomorrow.

• Structure: ask + object + to + V1 — "asked us to complete", "asked him to wait", "asked them to leave". (हमें होमवर्क पूरा करने को कहा)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "completing" (gerund/present participle) would be correct only after a preposition used as a preposition, e.g., "look forward to completing", not after the infinitive marker.

• Option 3 "completed" (V3/past form) and Option 4 "completes" (singular present) cannot follow the infinitive "to".

NOTE

• Verbs commonly followed by object + to-infinitive: ask, tell, advise, allow, request, order, permit, encourage, force, want, expect, persuade, remind, warn.

• Distinguish: "to" as an infinitive marker takes V1 (want to go), while "to" as a preposition takes the -ing form (used to, look forward to, object to, be accustomed to).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

He was not able to answer as the question was ambiguous.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Clear.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ambiguous" means having more than one possible meaning; unclear, vague and open to different interpretations. Its antonym is "clear" — easy to understand and having only one meaning. (अस्पष्ट / द्विअर्थी का विलोम — स्पष्ट)

◦ Example: His ambiguous reply confused everyone, so we asked for a clear answer.

• The sentence supports this: because the question was ambiguous (unclear), he could not answer it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Deep" refers to depth/profundity, not clarity.

• Option 3 "Superficial" means shallow or surface-level — it is not the opposite of ambiguous.

• Option 4 "Unsuitable" means not appropriate — unrelated to the idea of clarity.

NOTE

• Synonyms of ambiguous: vague, unclear, obscure, equivocal, cryptic, doubtful, hazy.

• Antonyms of ambiguous: clear, explicit, unambiguous, definite, obvious, lucid, precise.

• Related word: ambivalent (having mixed or contradictory feelings) — often confused with "ambiguous" in exams.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

The allowance that is given by a husband to his wife on separation
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Alimony.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Alimony" is the one-word substitute for the allowance/maintenance that a husband is legally bound to pay his wife after a divorce or judicial separation. (गुज़ारा भत्ता / निर्वाह भत्ता)

◦ Example: The court ordered him to pay monthly alimony to his former wife.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Matrimonial" is an adjective meaning relating to marriage — not an allowance.

• Option 3 "Affianced" means engaged to be married (betrothed).

• Option 4 "Dowry" is the property or money brought by a bride to her husband at the time of marriage — it is not paid on separation. (Note: the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 bans dowry in India.)

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes for SSC: Bigamy (marrying while already married to another), Polygamy (having many spouses), Monogamy (marriage to one person at a time), Celibacy (abstaining from marriage), Misogamy (hatred of marriage), Divorce (legal dissolution of marriage).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Forests provide essential ecosystem services (1)__________ benefit both the environment and human society. One crucial service is carbon sequestration, as forests absorb and store large amounts of carbon dioxide, helping mitigate climate change. Additionally, forests regulate water cycles (2)__________ influencing precipitation patterns and maintaining water quality. (3)__________, forests offer recreational opportunities, cultural significance, and economic benefits through timber production and (4)__________. Thus, preserving and sustainably managing forests is imperative for maintaining these (5)__________ ecosystem services.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. that.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank must join the noun "services" to the verb "benefit", so a relative pronoun is needed. "That" (or "which") correctly introduces a relative clause describing the ecosystem services.

◦ Correct: Forests provide essential ecosystem services that benefit both the environment and human society.

• "That" here refers back to the plural noun "services" and acts as the subject of the verb "benefit".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "than" is used only for comparison (bigger than, more than) — there is no comparison here.

• Option 3 "then" is an adverb of time meaning "at that time / next".

• Option 4 "this" is a demonstrative used with a singular noun and cannot connect the two clauses.

NOTE

• Do not confuse than (comparison) with then (time). Relative pronouns: who (persons), which (things/animals), that (persons or things), whose (possession), whom (object form).

• "Carbon sequestration" mentioned in the passage means the capture and long-term storage of carbon dioxide — a key climate-change concept.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Forests provide essential ecosystem services (1)__________ benefit both the environment and human society. One crucial service is carbon sequestration, as forests absorb and store large amounts of carbon dioxide, helping mitigate climate change. Additionally, forests regulate water cycles (2)__________ influencing precipitation patterns and maintaining water quality. (3)__________, forests offer recreational opportunities, cultural significance, and economic benefits through timber production and (4)__________. Thus, preserving and sustainably managing forests is imperative for maintaining these (5)__________ ecosystem services.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. by.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is followed by the gerund "influencing", and the sense required is the means or method through which forests regulate water cycles. The preposition that expresses means/method before an "-ing" form is "by".

◦ Correct: ... forests regulate water cycles by influencing precipitation patterns and maintaining water quality.

• Structure: by + V-ing = "through the act of doing something" (by working hard, by reading daily, by influencing).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "off" indicates separation or removal (take off, get off) and does not fit.

• Option 2 "about" indicates a topic (talk about, think about), not a means.

• Option 4 "between" indicates a position among two things and is grammatically impossible here.

NOTE

• Prepositions followed by the gerund (V-ing): by, for, of, in, on, without, after, before, instead of, in spite of. Example: "He succeeded by working hard", "She left without saying goodbye".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Forests provide essential ecosystem services (1)__________ benefit both the environment and human society. One crucial service is carbon sequestration, as forests absorb and store large amounts of carbon dioxide, helping mitigate climate change. Additionally, forests regulate water cycles (2)__________ influencing precipitation patterns and maintaining water quality. (3)__________, forests offer recreational opportunities, cultural significance, and economic benefits through timber production and (4)__________. Thus, preserving and sustainably managing forests is imperative for maintaining these (5)__________ ecosystem services.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Moreover.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence in the blank adds one more benefit of forests (recreation, cultural significance, economic benefits) to the benefits already mentioned. Therefore an additive linker is needed, and "Moreover" (meaning "in addition; besides") fits perfectly.

◦ Correct: Moreover, forests offer recreational opportunities, cultural significance, and economic benefits ...

• The comma after the blank also shows that a conjunctive adverb such as "Moreover / Furthermore / In addition" is required, not a subordinating conjunction.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "As long as" expresses a condition (as long as you study, you will pass) and needs a following clause.

• Option 3 "Whatever" is a relative/indefinite pronoun and makes no sense at the start of this sentence.

• Option 4 "Though" expresses contrast/concession, but the passage is adding, not contrasting.

NOTE

• Linkers by function: Addition — moreover, furthermore, besides, in addition, also. Contrast — however, nevertheless, though, whereas, on the contrary. Result — therefore, thus, hence, consequently. Example — for instance, such as, namely.

• Notice the passage ends with "Thus", a result linker, which supports the additive sense required in blank 3.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Forests provide essential ecosystem services (1)__________ benefit both the environment and human society. One crucial service is carbon sequestration, as forests absorb and store large amounts of carbon dioxide, helping mitigate climate change. Additionally, forests regulate water cycles (2)__________ influencing precipitation patterns and maintaining water quality. (3)__________, forests offer recreational opportunities, cultural significance, and economic benefits through timber production and (4)__________. Thus, preserving and sustainably managing forests is imperative for maintaining these (5)__________ ecosystem services.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. ecotourism.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is part of the phrase "economic benefits through timber production and _______", so the missing word must be another positive, income-generating activity connected with forests.

• "Ecotourism" means responsible tourism to natural areas that conserves the environment and benefits local people — exactly such a benefit. (पारिस्थितिकी पर्यटन)

◦ Correct: ... economic benefits through timber production and ecotourism.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "degradation" (deterioration of land/forests), Option 3 "deforestation" (cutting down of forests) and Option 4 "industrialisation" are all harmful to forests and contradict the positive tone of the passage.

• The passage is entirely about the benefits of forests and the need to preserve them, so a negative word cannot be the answer.

NOTE

• Environment vocabulary useful for SSC: carbon sequestration (storing CO₂), biodiversity, afforestation (planting new forests), reforestation (replanting cleared forests), sustainable management, ecosystem services.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Forests provide essential ecosystem services (1)__________ benefit both the environment and human society. One crucial service is carbon sequestration, as forests absorb and store large amounts of carbon dioxide, helping mitigate climate change. Additionally, forests regulate water cycles (2)__________ influencing precipitation patterns and maintaining water quality. (3)__________, forests offer recreational opportunities, cultural significance, and economic benefits through timber production and (4)__________. Thus, preserving and sustainably managing forests is imperative for maintaining these (5)__________ ecosystem services.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. vital.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank comes before the noun phrase "ecosystem services", so an adjective is required. "Vital" is the adjective meaning absolutely necessary; essential; extremely important. (अत्यावश्यक / महत्वपूर्ण)

◦ Correct: ... preserving and sustainably managing forests is imperative for maintaining these vital ecosystem services.

• The word also echoes "essential ecosystem services" used in the first line of the passage, keeping the passage consistent.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "vitalise" is a verb (to give life or energy to).

• Option 2 "vitally" is an adverb (vitally important) and cannot modify a noun.

• Option 3 "vitality" is a noun (energy, liveliness) and cannot qualify another noun here.

NOTE

• Word family: vital (adjective) – vitally (adverb) – vitality (noun) – vitalise/revitalise (verb).

• Rule: an adjective modifies a noun (vital services), an adverb modifies a verb/adjective/another adverb (vitally important). Synonyms of vital: essential, crucial, indispensable, imperative, key.
